title: H-1B Anxiety Spikes as Fees Soar and Fraud Probes Widen
excerpt: A $100,000 federal fee, Texas ghost-office investigations, and tech layoffs converge to rattle Indian visa holders
body:
**A Perfect Storm for Visa Workers**

The H-1B visa programme — long the primary conduit for Indian tech talent entering the American workforce — is under siege from multiple directions. A new $100,000 federal fee on fresh petitions has made sponsorship prohibitively expensive for smaller firms. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton is probing 30 North Texas companies for operating "ghost offices" to game the system. And ongoing tech-sector layoffs continue to leave visa holders scrambling for new sponsors within the 60-day grace period.

Indian nationals, who receive roughly 70% of all H-1B approvals, bear the brunt of each new restriction.

**Political Headwinds**

The debate has acquired fresh toxicity. Conservative commentator Christopher Rufo and allied lawmakers have amplified calls to slash the programme, framing it as a displacement mechanism for American workers. Meanwhile, USCIS has signalled that even previously approved cases may face reopening — an unprecedented step that has sent anxiety levels through the community.

**What It Means for the Diaspora**

For the estimated 600,000 Indians on H-1B status and millions more in the green-card backlog, the compounding pressures are existential. Higher costs deter employers from sponsoring, fraud crackdowns tighten adjudication standards, and layoff-triggered status gaps leave families one missed deadline from deportation. Community advocates are urging Congress to decouple the programme's legitimate economic function from its exploitation by bad actors.

nri_angle: With 70% of H-1B recipients being Indian, every fee hike, fraud probe, and policy tightening directly reshapes career and immigration timelines for hundreds of thousands of Indian-American families.
author: Diaspora Desk
